source.citation: "Chicago's Last Great War Dance." Chicagology, transcribing the Chicago Tribune of 14 August 1910, which prints John Dean Caton's written recollection of 18 August 1835, and, below it and unnamed, a first-person passage from an older book.

transcribes.note: Carries the one thing this dataset takes: on 18 August 1835 the procession crossed the North Branch bridge on foot in a crowd, then went south along West Water Street past the Green Tree and Wolf's Point taverns to the log raft bridge over the South Branch. That is the bridge standing, the bridge loaded, and the route of two streets, six and a half weeks after the scene date — see data/structures/north_branch_bridge.json. An identified eyewitness's own words at seventy-five years' remove, printed by a newspaper that neither dates nor documents the writing: near-primary recollection, rung 2.
transcribes.work: Chicago Tribune, 'Chicago's Last Great War Dance' — printing the recollection of Judge John Dean Caton, who saw it in his youth and wrote it out in old age

what_it_does_not_supply: any dimension, form or material of either bridge — Caton describes crossing them, not building them
a position for the North Branch bridge: the 'where the railroad bridge stands now' gloss is the 1910 newspaper's, not the witness's, and no placement here uses it
anything this project may depict of the event itself, which is under the AGENTS.md standing constraint
what_it_supplies: the North Branch bridge standing and carrying a crowd on 18 August 1835
the raft bridge over the South Branch standing the same day, and its position relative to the Sauganash
the route west along the north bank and south along West Water Street past the Green Tree and Wolf's Point taverns
